flags.source_says: Source Q30 (p.27) has the same table (Rare <1 in 10y; Unlikely 3-10y; Possible 1-3y; Likely >=1/yr). The source presents it as an example anchoring, so the JSON copied it faithfully.
flags.derivation: The key (a) is correct: anchoring each level to a frequency band is the right design choice. The worked table, however, is the only concrete likelihood scale shown to the candidate, and its bands and labels differ from the curriculum's four-point scale (Chapelle, ORR Ch.4; notes/FRM_Consolidated_Vol1/ch/32_OR_ORR4.tex lines 122-141). The curriculum scale is Likely = once per year or more (>50%), Possible = 1-5 years (20-50%), Unlikely = 1 in 5-20 years (5-20%), Remote = <1 in 20 years (<5%). A candidate who memorises 'Rare < once in ten years' or 'Possible = 1-3 years' will get a recall question on the curriculum scale wrong. The answer is unaffected.
